title: perf(canary): automated detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce manual detection of performance regressions during canary rollouts by adding an automated detector that watches latency and throughput signals and wires in rollout guards (hysteresis, minimum sample sizes, fallback to stable variant). This PR implements: 1) a detector service that continuously computes per-route latency/throughput deltas against baseline canary windows, with configurable sensitivity and minimum sample sizes; 2) a hysteresis-based rollout guard that prevents automatic promotion when transient spikes are detected and triggers automatic rollback when sustained regressions exceed thresholds; 3) integration hooks with the deployment orchestration so canaries can opt into automated gating; 4) observability dashboards and alerts for SRE and product owners. Implementation notes: - Detector runs as part of perf-canary service and subscribes to the canary metrics stream (summaries every 10s). - Comparison uses median and 95th percentile windows plus throughput checks; both latency and throughput regressions are considered. - Hysteresis window is configurable per-route via rollout policy. - Default behavior is opt-in (flag off for existing canaries), can be enabled via route config. Testing: unit tests for detector stats, integration tests against synthetic traces, end-to-end canary smoke with sandbox. Checklist: - [x] detector core algorithm implemented - [x] rollout guard logic + hysteresis - [x] integration with orchestration API - [x] dashboards + alerts - [x] unit + integration + e2e tests - [x] docs updated (docs/perf-canary.md) Rollout plan: merge to main, enable feature-flag in staging, run 24h of canaries with synthetic traffic, enable for low-traffic routes, monitor dashboards, then progressive rollout to high-traffic routes.
